correctness.rationale: For length-n source and ordered palindromic duplicate lengths k then ell, the two legal start counts multiply to bound descendants by (n−k+1)(n+k−ell+1). On an all-distinct-letter word, every original first occurrence remains first after insertions, so the final word uniquely partitions into copy gaps. If two gaps are occupied, their unequal sizes k,ell identify the first gap and site, then recover the intermediate word and second site. If only one gap, its index identifies the first duplication; the h copies before second insertion give pairwise distinct outputs: for 1<=h<hprime compare at gap position h, and compare h=0 separately using ell>=2. Therefore no two histories collide. Exact independent enumeration checked 369 legal (n,k,ell) triples and 7227 outputs. Boundary counterexamples for ell=1 and ell=k correctly delimit the theorem. This is a uniform proof for q>=n, not just the finite enumeration.
residual_risks: No assertion for q<n, equal prescribed lengths, second length one, unordered operations, or more than two steps.
